q: 1. The angle of intersection of a curve is the angle between
options: prolongation of back tangent and forward tangent
explain: The angle of intersection is the angle between the prolongation of the back (rear) tangent and the forward tangent, measured at the point of intersection of the two straights.

q: 2. When the curve is to be set out over a rough ground, the method used is ...............
explain: On rough ground where chaining is difficult, methods that use angles or optical distance measurement (two-theodolite or tacheometric) are preferred.

q: 3. The theodolite method off setting out a curve involves ...............
explain: Theodolite methods (like the two-theodolite method) primarily rely on angular observations to define points on the curve.

q: 4. A curve of varying radius is known as ...............
explain: A transition curve is designed to have a radius that changes continuously (usually from infinity to a fixed radius) to provide a gradual change in centrifugal force.

q: 5. Setting out of a simple curve by two theodolite method does not require ...............
explain: The two-theodolite method allows for curve setting using only angular intersection, meaning no chaining (linear measurement) along the curve is needed.

q: 6. In a reverse curve, the super elevation provided at the point of reverse curvature is ...............
options: dependent on the element of reverse curve
explain: At the point of reverse curvature, the direction of curvature changes; therefore, the super-elevation must pass through zero as it switches sides.

q: 7. Different grades are joined together by ...............
explain: A vertical curve is used to provide a smooth transition between two different gradients (grades) on a road or railway.

q: 8. The curve composed of two arcs of different radii having their centers on the opposite side of the curve, is known ...............
explain: A reverse curve (S-curve) consists of two circular arcs bending in opposite directions with centers on opposite sides of the common tangent.

q: 9. Point of tangency is the ...............
options: common point where the radius changes
common point where the radius and direction changes
explain: The Point of Curve (PC) is the start, and the Point of Tangency (PT) is the end of the curve where it joins the forward tangent.

q: 10. In a simple curve, 'External distance' is the distance between ...............
options: vertex and middle point of the curve
vertex and the centre of the curve
point of curve and point of tangency
explain: The external distance (apex distance) is the distance from the intersection point (vertex) to the apex of the curve.

q: 11. The approximate formula for radial or perpendicular offsets from the tangent is
explain: For short distances (x), the perpendicular offset (O) is approximately $O = x^2 / 2R$.

q: 12. Perpendicular offset from a tangent to the junction of a transition curve and circular curve is equal to
explain: In the geometry of a transition curve, the offset at the end of the transition curve (where it meets the circular curve) is four times the shift 's'.

q: 13. The properties of autogenous curve for automobiles are given by
explain: Bernoulli's lemniscate is considered the ideal transition curve for highways where the deflection angle is large, as it mimics the natural path of a vehicle's steering.

q: 14. If D is the angle of deflection of a simple curve of radius R, the length of its long chord, is
explain: The long chord is the straight line connecting the start and end of the curve. Its length is calculated as $2R sin(Delta/2)$, where $Delta$ (or D) is the deflection angle.

q: 15. The chord of a curve less than peg interval, is known as
explain: A sub-chord is any chord shorter than the standard 'normal' chord length (usually the peg interval).

q: 16. The spiral angle of a transition curve will be given by the equation
explain: The spiral (deflection) angle of a transition curve at any point is given by the formula phi = L2/(2*R*Ls) which, at the end of a full transition curve of length L, reduces to the standard form L2/2R (for the total spiral length).

q: 17. Rankine's deflection angle in minutes is obtained by multiplying the length of the chord by .............
options: square of the degree of the curve
inverse of the degree of the curve
explain: Rankine's method relates the deflection angle directly to the chord length and the degree of the curve (or radius).

q: 18. An ideal transition curve is .............
explain: The clothoid (or Euler spiral) is considered the ideal transition curve because its curvature increases linearly with distance.

q: 19. Shift of a curve, is .............
explain: The shift (S) required for a transition curve is calculated using the formula S = L²/24R.

q: 20. A reverse curve consists of
options: a single curve of a circle connecting two straights
two arcs of different radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal or different radii bending in the opposite directions
explain: A reverse curve is composed of two circular arcs (of equal or different radii) that curve in opposite directions, joined at a common tangent point.

q: 21. When the centers of the arcs lie on the opposite sides of the common tangent at the junction of the two curves, it is known as a
explain: This specific geometric arrangement, where the centres of curvature of the two joined arcs lie on opposite sides of their common tangent, defines a reverse curve.

q: 22. A simple circular curve is designated by the
options: angle subtended at the centre by a chord of any length
angle subtended at the centre by a chord of a particular length
explain: A simple circular curve is conventionally designated by its 'degree of curve', which is the angle subtended at the centre by a chord of one particular standard length (e.g., 30 m or 100 ft).

q: 23. The degree of the curve is the angle subtended by a chord of length.
explain: As per this text's convention, the degree of a curve is defined as the angle subtended at the centre by a standard chord length of 30 m.

q: 24. When R is the radius of the curve (in meters), D is the degree of curve (in degrees) and length of the chord is 30 m, then the relation between R and D is
explain: For a 30 m chord definition of degree of curve, the standard relation is R = 1720/D (approximately, derived from R = (chord/2)/sin(D/2) for small D).

q: 25. The angle between the back tangent and forward tangent of a curve is known as
explain: The angle subtended at the centre of the curve between the back tangent and the forward tangent (or equivalently between the two radii to the tangent points) is called the central angle.

q: 26. The angle by which the forward tangent deflects from the back tangent of a curve is called
explain: The deflection angle is, by definition, the angle by which the forward tangent direction deflects from the direction of the back tangent.

q: 27. A deflection angle is
options: more than 90 deg but less than 180 deg
equal to the difference between the angle of intersection and 180 deg
equal to the difference between the angle of intersection and 360 deg
explain: The deflection angle and the angle of intersection are supplementary, so the deflection angle equals 180 deg minus the angle of intersection.

q: 28. The length of peg interval for flat curves is
explain: For flat (large radius) curves, pegs are usually set out at the full standard chord interval of 30 m, as used for the degree-of-curve definition.

q: 29. When the length of a chord is less than the peg interval, it is known as
explain: A chord shorter than the standard peg interval (used typically at the beginning or end of a curve) is called a sub-chord.

q: 30. The total length of the curve is equal to
explain: The length of a circular curve (arc) subtending an angle phi (in degrees) at the centre, with radius R, is given by L = pi*R*phi/180.

q: 31. Different grades are jointed together by
explain: Vertical curves are used to smoothly join two different longitudinal gradients (grades) on a road or railway alignment.

q: 32. 'Point of curve' is
explain: The 'point of curve' refers to the point of commencement of the curve, i.e., where the curve begins (tangent point at the start).

q: 33. The angle of intersection of a curve is the angle between
explain: As stated in Q12, the angle of intersection of a curve is the angle between the (prolongation of) back tangent and the forward tangent.

q: 34. An ideal vertical curve to join two gradients, is
explain: A simple parabolic curve is considered ideal for vertical curves joining two different road/rail gradients, since it provides a constant rate of change of grade.

q: 35. A simple circular curve is designated by .............
options: angle subtended at the centre by a chord of any length
angle subtended at the centre by a chord of particular length
explain: In engineering practice, a curve is often designated by the degree of the curve, which is the angle subtended at the center by a standard chord (usually 20m or 30m).

q: 36. The 'point of curve' of a simple circular curve is .............
explain: The point of curve (PC) is the point where the straight alignment (tangent) ends and the circular curve begins; it is the point of commencement.

q: 37. Designation of a curve is made by .............
options: angle subtended by a chord of any length
angle subtended by an arc of specified length
explain: In engineering practice, a curve is primarily designated either by its Radius (R) or by its Degree of Curvature (D).

q: 38. If D is the degree of the curve of radius R, the exact length of its specified chord, is
options: radius of the curve × sine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × sine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × cosine of half the degree
diameter of the curve × tangent of half the degree
explain: Using trigonometry, the chord length $L = 2R sin(D/2)$. Since $2R$ is the diameter, the expression is diameter $	imes sin(D/2)$.

q: 39. The shape of vertical curve generally provided is
explain: Parabolic curves are preferred for vertical curves because they provide a constant rate of change of grade, leading to a smoother transition.

q: 40. Overturning of vehicles on a curve can be avoided by using
explain: 0) A **transition curve** (spiral) gradually changes the radius from infinity to a fixed value, allowing the centrifugal force to build up slowly and providing space to apply super-elevation, which prevents overturning. 1) Vertical curves handle changes in slope (up/down), not lateral stability. 2) and 3) These are types of circular curves that still have an abrupt change in curvature at the tangent point, which is where overturning risk is highest.

q: 41. When R is radius (m) and D is degree of curve, relation for 30 m chord is
explain: For a 30m chord, $R = (30 \times 180) / (\pi \times D) \approx 1718.87 / D$. This is usually rounded to $1720/D$ in many textbooks.

q: 42. The angle between the back tangent and forward tangent of a curve is
explain: The central angle (or angle of intersection) is the angle between the two tangents at the point of intersection (PI).

q: 43. In a lemniscate curve, the angle between the tangent at the end of the polar ray and the tangent at the commencement of the curve (i.e., straight) is ............. the angle between the polar ray and the straight .............
explain: In a lemniscate curve, the polar deflection angle ($\alpha$) is related to the total deflection angle ($\delta$) such that $\delta = 3\alpha$.

q: 44. A reverse curve consists of .............
options: a single curve of a circle connecting two straights
two arcs of different radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal radii bending in the same direction
two arcs of equal or different radii bending in the opposite direction
explain: A reverse curve (S-curve) consists of two circular arcs with centers on opposite sides of a common tangent.

q: 45. If the radius of a simple curve is R, the length of the chord for calculating offsets by the method of chords produced, should not exceed .............
explain: For the method of chords produced, the chord length is generally kept within R/20 to ensure that the approximation (arc length ≈ chord length) remains accurate for plotting.

q: 46. The angle by which the forward tangent deflects from the back tangent of a curve is known as .............
explain: The deflection angle is the angle at which the new direction (forward tangent) deviates from the extension of the previous direction (back tangent).

q: 47. A deflection angle is .............
options: equal to the difference between the angel of intersection and 180°
equal to the difference between the angel of intersection and 360°
explain: The sum of the deflection angle and the internal angle of intersection ($I$) equals 180°. Therefore, Deflection Angle = $180° - I$.

q: 48. An angle of deflection right, may be directly obtained by setting the instrument to read .............
explain: If you zero the instrument on the back sight and then turn to the next station, the resulting clockwise reading is the deflection angle.

q: 49. The perpendicular offset from a tangent to the junction of transition curve and circular curve is equal to .............
explain: This offset value is mathematically derived for a spiral transition curve to ensure a smooth change in curvature; it is often noted as $Y = L^2 / (24R)$.

q: 50. The shift of a curve is equal to .............
explain: The 'shift' is the distance by which the circular curve must be moved inward to accommodate the transition curve, calculated as $S = L^2 / (24R)$.
